topic.name: Combining Radical Expressions Using the Product Rule

question.explanation: We perform the multiplication under a single radical and then simplify the result: \[ \eqalign{ 2\sqrt{8ab^3} \cdot 3\sqrt{9b}&=\\[3pt] 2\cdot3\sqrt{8ab^3\cdot9b}&=\\[3pt] 6\sqrt{72ab^4}&=\\[3pt] 6\sqrt{36b^4\cdot 2a}&=\\[3pt] 6\sqrt{(6b^2)^2\cdot 2a}&=\\[3pt] 6\sqrt{(6b^2)^2}\cdot\sqrt{ 2a}&=\\[3pt] 6\cdot |6b^2|\cdot\sqrt{2a}&=\\[3pt] 6\cdot |6|\cdot |b^2|\cdot\sqrt{2a}&=\\[3pt] 6\cdot 6\cdot|b^2|\cdot\sqrt{2a} } \] A squared number is always positive or zero, and the absolute value of any positive (or zero) number is itself, so we have \[ \eqalign{ 6\cdot 6\cdot|b^2|\cdot\sqrt{2a}&=\\[3pt] 36\cdot b^2\cdot\sqrt{2a}&=\\[3pt] 36b^2\sqrt{2a}. } \]

example.title: Combining Radical Expressions Using the Rules of Absolute Value

question.explanation:
We perform the multiplication under a single radical and then simplify the result: \[ \eqalign{ \sqrt{6a^3b} \cdot \sqrt{15abc} &= \\[3pt] \sqrt{6a^3b \cdot 15abc} &= \\[3pt] \sqrt{90a^4b^2c} &= \\[3pt] \sqrt{9a^4b^2 \cdot 10c} &= \\[3pt] \sqrt{(3a^2b)^2 \cdot 10c} &= \\[3pt] 3 \cdot |a^2| \cdot |b| \cdot \sqrt{10c} } \]

A squared number is always positive or zero, and the absolute value of any positive (or zero) number is itself, so we have that $|a^2|=a^2$ and $|b| = b.$ Therefore, our final answer is \[ \eqalign{ 3 \cdot |a^2| \cdot |b| \cdot \sqrt{10c} &= \\[3pt] 3a^2b\sqrt{10c}&. } \]
